To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Camassa-- Holm equation is a well posed and unique continuation model.
the Camassa-- Holm equation is not only a model of permanent waves, but also a model of breaking waves.

the periodic Camassa--Holms system does not have nontrivial global strong solutions vanishing in at most one point and that the Camassa--Homs equation with zero boundary conditions does not have global nontrivial strong solutions vanishing at both ends.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the Camassa--Holv equation, which is a nonlinear partial differential equation of the KdV type.
the analysis of the Cauchy problem and the unique continuation problem in the class of periodic solutions of the periodic rod equations.

the study of the long-time behavior of solutions to a class of nonlinear hyperbolic equations, including the Camassa-Holm and the Hunter-Saxton equations, arising in the description of the motion of elastic rods, in the case when a localized perturbation of the equilibrium is introduced.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of the periodic and non-periodic rod models, the Camassa--H\"ormann equation is the only model which admits nontrivial global strong solutions.
a hyperelastic rod or a ring with non-trivial initial data cannot be at rest for an extended period of time, unless its initial data are identically zero.
the only periodic or non-periodic global solutions vanishing in at most one point are the zero solutions, which are not physically relevant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the periodic rod model is a well-posed system, while the non-periodic rod model is ill-posed.
the Camassa-- Holm equation is the only physically relevant model of a periodic elastic rod, in the sense that all other models are unstable.
the Camassa-Holm equation is not a model of a hyperelastic rod.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rod equation is a nonlocal model for which the local-in-space approach to the analysis of wave propagation is not adequate.

the presence of the hyperbolic term in the equation, which is responsible for the wave propagation, is crucial to the non-uniqueness of the periodic rod model, and that the same phenomenon cannot take place for the Camassa-Holm equation.
the Camassa--Holv equation is not a good model to describe the dynamics of hyperelastic rods.
